newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share index barely up on blue chip losses.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share index barely up on blue chip losses.

text.p: Blue chips lost heavily on Friday in Nigerian share trading, leaving the all-share index marginally changed, traders said.
The index closed at 6635.21 from 6634.78 on Thursday.
Heavy selling saw prices of brewers and conglomerates slide, showing they were still under pressure by investors offloading.
Oil shares, the toast of the market, made modest advances despite a 21.7 percent drop in the nine-month result of Mobil.
"It was in line with the market expectation," one trader said, blaming it on low profit margin plaguing the oil sector.
"But oil shares are not likely to stagnate for long because investors demand for them is inexhaustible," he said.
Nigerian Breweries recorded Friday's heaviest fall, down 30 kobo at 10.20 naira after first touching 10.00 naira.
The company has lost almost 50 percent of its value since the start of the year due partly to falling demand for beer and because of large volumes of its shares flooding the market.
The same reason is given for the drop in Guinness by 10 kobo to 6.90 naira on Friday from its peak this year of 12.88 naira.

"These shares are getting to the point at which they will begin to look up again," said one trader. "It is a good time to buy them because the companies are still well managed and are in a position to ride out the problems facing them," he added.

Lever Brothers had its biggest one-day fall, sliding 15 kobo to 25.35 naira. UAC was five kobo lower at 9.40 naira. Union Bank and Afribank were five down at 7.30 naira and 5.00 naira respectively. But FSB Bank surged 15 kobo to 4.95 naira.
Traders said construction and insurance stocks were poised to continue their good run. Cappa and D'Alberto climbed 10 kobo to 8.90 naira and G. Cappa added same to 9.40 naira.
West African Portland Cement also rose 20 kobo to 37.20 naira on rising demand, traders said.
